title: Optimizing Mutual Fund Portfolio Management through the Application of Advanced Soft Computing Techniques
journal_or_venue: 2024 Third International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Information and Communication Technologies (ICEEICT)
abstract_summary: This paper proposes an integrated quantum-inspired framework combining a Quantum Neural Network (QNN) for performance prediction with a Quantum-Inspired Evolutionary Algorithm (QEA) for portfolio optimization to improve mutual fund management. Empirical results reported show improved forecast accuracy and decision-making versus traditional methods (mean MAPE 5.45% vs 5.68%), suggesting the approach can enhance risk-adjusted returns and responsiveness to market dynamics.
methodology_description: The authors propose an integrated, quantum-inspired framework that combines a Quantum-Inspired Evolutionary Algorithm (QEA) for portfolio optimization with a Quantum Neural Network (QNN) for portfolio performance prediction. The workflow begins with data collection of firm-level financial attributes (e.g., growth %, total funding, valuation, revenue, growth rates, and historical returns for a set of companies) and proceeds with data pre-processing: outlier detection/removal using the interquartile range (IQR) rule, min-max normalization to scale features to [0,1], and missing-value imputation (mean/median imputation is mentioned). The QEA is used to explore portfolio allocation configurations using quantum-inspired representations and evolutionary operators (selection, crossover, mutation) across iterative generations to find optimal or near-optimal portfolios while accounting for investor preferences, risk-adjusted returns and diversification. Each candidate portfolio produced by the QEA is evaluated by the QNN which is trained on historical financial data and incorporates quantum-inspired notions (e.g., qubit-like representations and quantum gate analogues in its architecture) to predict expected returns and risk measures. A feedback loop is established: QEA proposes portfolios → QNN predicts performance → predictions form fitness assessments that steer QEA search; actual portfolio outcomes (when available) are used to further refine and retrain the QNN, creating an adaptive, dynamic optimization–prediction loop. The approach was implemented as a simulation using Python and compared against traditional methods (baseline portfolio/prediction approaches) using prediction accuracy metrics (Mean Absolute Percentage Error - MAPE) and per-company predicted vs actual returns.

pipeline_steps: 1) Data collection of firm financials and historical returns.
2) Data cleaning and preprocessing: outlier removal (IQR), min-max normalization, missing-value imputation.
3) Initialize QEA population of candidate portfolio allocations using quantum-inspired encoding.
4) For each generation: apply evolutionary operators (selection, crossover, mutation) to evolve the population toward higher fitness.
5) For each candidate portfolio, pass portfolio configuration/features to the QNN to obtain predicted performance (expected return and risk).
6) Compute fitness of each portfolio based on QNN predictions and investor/risk preferences; use fitness to guide QEA evolution.
7) Repeat generations until stopping criteria (not specified) are met.
8) Optionally use realized portfolio outcomes to retrain/refine the QNN (feedback loop).
9) Compare final predicted returns against actual returns and baseline traditional methods (compute MAPE).

results_summary: The paper proposes an integrated quantum-inspired framework that pairs a Quantum Neural Network (QNN) for portfolio performance prediction with a Quantum-Inspired Evolutionary Algorithm (QEA) for portfolio optimization. Implemented in Python and tested on a set of companies, the framework produced a modest improvement in forecast accuracy versus a Traditional Method (mean MAPE 5.45% vs 5.68%). The paper also presents descriptive analyses of industry valuations, company funding, and projected revenues for the dataset. Many broader claims about computational efficiency, exponential speed-ups, and transformative impacts of quantum principles are presented as motivations or expectations rather than demonstrated outcomes in the reported experiments.
